note: Literature systematically demonstrates a clear divergence between biallelic loss-of-function variants causing early childhood neurodevelopmental arteriopathy and biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants manifesting as adult-onset CADASIL phenocopy.

evidence.text: A systematic cohort analysis verified distinct genotype-phenotype correlations: biallelic loss-of-function variants lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder marked by spasticity and childhood-onset stroke, whereas biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants present with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and typical CADASIL spectrum phenotype.

source.title: Clinical and neuroradiological spectrum of biallelic variants in NOTCH3
source.quote: Biallelic loss-of-function variants (26 patients) lead to a neurodevelopmental disorder characterised by spasticity, childhood-onset stroke, and periatrial white matter volume loss resembling periventricular leukomalacia. Conversely, patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants (24 patients) fall within CADASIL spectrum phenotype with early adulthood onset stroke, dementia, and deep white matter lesions without significant volume loss.

numbers.metric: patients with biallelic cysteine-involving missense variants

evidence.text: Patients with biallelic cysteine-sparing/loss-of-function NOTCH3 variants presented in early infancy (9 to 14 months) with developmental delay, seizures, and a vascular leukoencephalopathy distinct from classic CADASIL.

source.title: Early-onset vascular leukoencephalopathy caused by bi-allelic NOTCH3 variants
source.quote: The patients presented at 9 to 14 months of age with developmental delay, seizures, or both. The disease course was characterized by cognitive impairment and variably recurrent strokes, migraine attacks, and seizures... Bi-allelic cysteine-sparing NOTCH3 variants in exons 1, 32, and 33 were found.
